observed_defect: The user-provided Google Chrome/Facebook result showed that the in-page request did not ask for source lookup and that the context panel was absent.
fix_implemented: The Facebook in-page preview now exposes an explicit approved-source/fact-check lookup checkbox and persists it. Both the in-page result and popup render the backend context again. The rebuilt extension still requires Chrome reload and hands-on retesting.
reason: An actual Facebook post was analyzed in Google Chrome on the previous build and exposed the lookup/context defect. The corrected build has automated component, contract and isolated popup evidence, but has not yet been reloaded and retested by the user in Google Chrome.
automated_evidence_that_does_not_count_a: Headless Chrome rendered the real English and Tagalog React result components without horizontal clipping.
The extension API client and background transport reached the live local API.
The corrected popup passed an isolated Microsoft Edge Chromium regression with the context panel visible.
A live API request using the public text visible in the user screenshot returned one related result from an approved publisher; Google Fact Check legitimately returned no matching review.
manual_steps_remaining: Open chrome://extensions and enable Developer mode.
Reload the existing SuriPH extension, or choose Load unpacked and select chrome-extension/dist.
Reload the Facebook tab so manifest version 1.2.1 and the new content script are active.
Open the green S control, review the text, enable the new approved-source/fact-check lookup checkbox, and analyze again.
Confirm that Context of the analyzed content is visible and that the related-source status no longer says lookup was off.
Check manual text, exact selected text, a recognized post caption, an image, and a short video; confirm the analyzed text before judging the prediction.
Switch English/Tagalog on the result and confirm the label, score, values, source titles, and analyzed text do not change.
